Building with Atomic

Describe a change, inspect the result, and move forward with a version you understand.

Build & refine · 4 min read

On this pageDescribe the behaviorRefine in small stepsReview the preview and checksUnderstand version historyPrepare a version to share
Before you startAtomic is preparing for early access. The examples on this website are local demonstrations using sample data; they do not generate or host an app.

Describe the behavior

Explain what a person should be able to do and what should happen next. “Let the owner confirm a booking” gives a clearer target than “make it more professional.” Separate functional requests from visual refinements when possible.

Refine in small steps

After a first version, ask for a focused improvement. Adjust a form, simplify a navigation path, or clarify a confirmation message. Review the changed area before combining it with the next request.

When a client submits a booking request, show the selected service and time in the confirmation. Make clear that the owner still needs to approve it.

Review the preview and checks

Try the app as each kind of user. Check empty states, invalid input, repeated submissions, and narrow screens. Review available build checks, but remember that a successful build does not establish that permissions, business rules, or security are correct.

Use sample data during development. Avoid including passwords, payment details, or unnecessary personal information in your prompts.

Understand version history

Atomic’s workflow includes verified source history and frontend release rollback. Returning to an earlier source version or frontend release does not restore your app’s business data. Database changes and data recovery need their own plan.

Prepare a version to share

When the core workflow is useful, work through the publishing guide. Keep a record of what you tested and the known limitations of the version you are sharing.
